active_initiatives.name: Dyson Hope Reels — Own-Account Performance Capture + Weekly Analysis

contract.runner_scope: Engineering + Research-buildable. A local-scheduled (launchd) daily capture of the CEO's OWN Instagram professional accounts' authoritative Reel Insights via the official Meta-native Instagram API with Instagram Login, normalized to account-partitioned Obsidian-friendly snapshot CSVs plus append-only history ledgers, written atomically by a single-writer job. JasonOS owns the schedule and OAuth token lifecycle; Meta is the first-party source of record. Initial accounts are @dysonhopemusic and @sigil.zero.records; @jasoncookdesign is a future account to add once it exists. Collection is an ApifySource's sibling — a GraphApiSource behind the same provider-neutral MetricsSource interface.
contract.stop_line: Read-only Insights capture of the CEO's OWN professional accounts — no posting, no publishing, no comment/message actions, no account mutation. The app requests only read scopes (instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_manage_insights). Metrics INFORM the CEO; they never trigger autonomous strategy or content changes. The access token is a secret and is handled as one (never in plist, logs, ticket text, or commits). No third-party scraping in this initiative's data path.

GAP-216's fix required update_scheduled_task (Cowork-only) to sync the canonical operations/assets/jasonos-operations-backup.SKILL.md source to the live deployed Cowork scheduled-task prompt -- native Claude Code cannot perform that sync, so a source-only fix silently leaves the OLD (defective) prompt running until someone remembers the manual step or Security Steward's weekly drift check (PCR-OPS-008) catches it. CEO asked whether the scheduled task could just read the source live instead of keeping two manually-synced copies; President Agent's counter-proposal: a fetch-and-confirm pattern rather than a bare live read -- each Cowork-run scheduled task's Step 0 fetches its own canonical SKILL.md source, hashes it, and either proceeds only on a match to an approved value or explicitly reports/escalates a mismatch instead of silently running stale (or silently running unreviewed-new) instructions -- preserves the existing deploy-review gate (an edit doesn't go live merely by being saved) while catching drift automatically and immediately instead of relying on a human noticing or a weekly sweep. CEO's stated alternative, which they are open to considering and specifically framed as a possible full replacement rather than a complement to the above: deprecate ALL Cowork-run scheduled tasks and replace them with native launchd invocation on the Mac mini, motivated by making JasonOS more provider-agnostic (a stated organizational goal) -- this would eliminate the two-copy/sync-gap problem class entirely (no separate Cowork-deployed prompt to drift from source), at the cost of whatever Cowork-only capabilities (e.g. Gmail/Drive/Shopify MCP connectors) any given scheduled task currently depends on, which would need per-task auditing before a migration could be scoped. Not admitted as work: this is an architecture-direction question for the CEO to decide (incremental sync-gate vs. structural migration), not yet a scoped, approved piece of work.

pending_notes.summary: infrastructure-health-policy.md scores dashboard-publisher liveness off status.json's generated_at against a 2-hour threshold, but generated_at is not a heartbeat: the publisher only rewrites status.json when the projection CHANGES ('status.json: no-diff; trigger skipped'), so on a quiet system the field ages past the threshold while the daemon is demonstrably healthy. Observed live this sweep: publisher last ran 2026-08-06T10:12:37Z (59m ago, clean, both no-diff), yet generated_at reads 2026-08-06T08:12:34Z — 2h59m, which scores a Medium staleness breach if the policy is applied literally. Compounding: the plist's own StartInterval backstop is 7200s = exactly the 2h threshold, so even a changed-projection run has zero jitter headroom. Verified at source: publisher log, status.json mtime (08:12Z), and the matching relay commit 00939ab. Not admitted as work: no live control has failed — the daemon is running and the projection is current — and no delivery is blocked. Filed because the false-positive direction is the dangerous one for a liveness check: it trains the reader to discount the signal.
pending_notes.source: report-triage 2026-08-06 step 2k infrastructure health, verified against Logs/director-logs/engineering/dashboard-publisher.log and the publisher plist

Also cleared two orphaned loose-object tmp files in code/dysonhope/.git/objects that pre-existed this sweep and are consistent with the 07:12Z blog-drip publish. Not admitted as work: no live control failed, nothing was lost, and the repair path is a documented, working helper. Filed because the invariant's verb list is the thing that misled, and it is the same sentence a future agent will read.

PCR-OPS-077 (group portfolio initiatives into Programs, filed 2026-08-07, status Draft) carries work_class: maintenance_investment and production_or_maintenance: maintenance, but contains none of the five payback fields that class requires - expected production gain, payback horizon, estimated build effort, estimated carrying cost, payback result - plus no decision cycle. Verified at source, not just from the checker: a grep for 'payback', 'production gain', 'carrying cost', 'build effort' and 'decision cycle' across all 111 lines of the file returns zero hits, so the case is absent in prose too, not merely unfielded. This is the exact evidence the report-triage admission rule's fourth path (maintenance investment) is built on - a maintenance PCR with no payback case cannot consume a maintenance decision, because there is nothing to weigh. Mitigating and why this stays observation-only: the PCR is explicitly 'proposal only ... filed for review now and will be executed at a time of the CEO's choosing', so nothing is being admitted on it today, and contract conformance is observation-only under protocol v2.3 step 2c. Not admitted as work.

What has no owner is the alarm: a failed daily business-continuity backup currently produces no escalation, no director-log entry, and no distinguishable signal. NOT ADMITTED AS WORK. A second consecutive failure, or any failure leaving the Drive copy inconsistent, satisfies protocol v2.3 admission path 2 and should be admitted then.

The daily operations backup rotates git-relay.log at ~07:41Z into Archive/Logs/engineering/<D>/git-relay-<D>.log, but that file is named for the date it was WRITTEN and covers <D-1>T07:41Z through <D>T07:41Z. Verified: git-relay-2026-08-12.log opens 'Log rotated 2026-08-11' and ends at 2026-08-12T07:40:57Z; the 2026-08-12T07:52Z events live in git-relay-2026-08-13.log. Any task running after 07:41Z that looks for yesterday's relay evidence in the archive named for yesterday will miss that day's final ~16 hours and see a false absence. This produced two incorrect escalations in the 2026-08-13 financial-state-backup run. Reasoning from absence in this archive requires naming the file searched and its coverage range.

Both escalations in the 2026-08-13 financial-analysis-log FSS entry are disconfirmed and should not be assigned. ESCALATION 1 ('the 2026-08-12 run did not fire; fault is in the scheduled-task invocation') is false: the run fired and errored — relay probe 20260812T075245Z-20a77140.result status=active 07:52:47Z, trigger 20260812T075247Z-fff748df.result status=error 07:53:17Z naming financial-state.yaml, and git-relay-2026-08-13.log lines 4728-4881 record the trigger, the precommand and 'backup aborted: UploadError: PATCH .../1fpba1URnt1iUJ-MTz7sMXZX8KhYXxQgu: [Errno 60] Operation timed out'. ESCALATION 2 (silent mirror staleness from an appProperties.sha256/body divergence) is structurally impossible: jasonos-drive-backup-runner.py _put() sends content and appProperties.sha256 in a single multipart PATCH. The real explanation is a partial 08-12 run — plan.updates is sorted and applied in order (attribution-rules.json, forecast-baseline-store.json, retention-log.md), so the first two were durably written before the timeout on the third, which is exactly why 08-13 saw those two 'unchanged' and retention-log.md 'updated'. The CONFIDENTIAL mirror is current, not stale. No Engineering assignment is warranted.

The CEO reported this session's commit_via_relay.py hand-off went through two malformed iterations before succeeding: (1) --push canonical against jasonos-operations, refused because that repo is single-origin (GAP-051: canonical is only valid for mirrored-governance repos; single-origin repos take --push true) -- the CLI's own --push help text lists 'canonical (upstream only; fork is a CEO-managed backup -- mirrored-governance repos, PCR-OPS-024)' distinctly from 'true (upstream+fork)', which names the distinction directly; (2) a directory-form --pathspec entry (operations/builds/fiction-development-system/modules/) refused with 'file-level pathspec required', which is not a new discovery -- governance/memory/relay-v128-path-limited-and-workers-event-driven.md already documents this exact constraint verbatim ('keep passing explicit space-separated file paths in --pathspec, never a directory or glob', GAP-127 residual) from a prior session. Both failures were avoidable: the CLI's own --help text and an existing memory entry already contained the correct answer before the command was ever typed. The commands were constructed from recalled pattern-memory of prior relay usage rather than by checking commit_via_relay.py --help (or the relevant memory file) against the specific repo/pathspec shape in hand. This is the second known recurrence of the directory-pathspec mistake specifically (the first is what produced the GAP-127/relay-v128 memory entry in the first place), suggesting the existing memory note alone is not reliably surfaced or consulted before a relay command is drafted. Recommendation: before constructing any commit_via_relay.py invocation, run --help (or grep the relay memory files) for the specific flags being used (--push mode for the target repo's topology; --pathspec shape) rather than reconstructing the command from session-to-session recall -- the authoritative spec is one cheap command away and guessing produces exactly this avoidable churn, doubly so when (as here) the guess repeats a mistake already once diagnosed and filed.

Consequence: if a mechanism were added, retired, or the 58 ceiling breached, status.json would continue to report at_ceiling 58/58 with a stale breakdown and no reader would see it from the dashboard. NOT admitted as a broken guardrail: the actual enforcement control is check-script-registry-coverage.py, which ran this sweep and correctly held the 58/58 one-in-one-out ceiling. Concrete miss: at 2026-08-17T23:59:51Z it hit 'ERROR: git fetch origin failed', appended a state-change entry, and sent an msmtp alert; it self-cleared to status=clean 15 minutes later at 2026-08-18T00:14:57Z. (2) check-scheduled-task-coverage.py exits 2 ('could not locate repo ... or scheduler path (None)') — fifth consecutive sweep since 2026-08-17T05:33Z; the checker resolves the scheduler at ~/Claude/Scheduled or /sessions/*/mnt/Claude/Scheduled and this session's granted folders are JasonOS, SandboxData and bin only, with no Claude mount. The durable finding is that a permanently-unreachable check has no disposition path — the Security Steward's standing question F6 ('what should a permanently unreachable check report?') has been re-raised in the sweep narrative on every one of those runs since 2026-07-31 and remains unanswered, so the estate carries two coverage controls whose result is structurally unknowable from the environment they are scheduled in, and only the sweep's prose records it.
